question.problem:
Daniel decides to go on a diet. The table below gives the rate $w(t)$, in pounds per week, at which he loses weight over a period of $7$ weeks.

| $t\,(\text{week})$ | $0$ | $1$ | $3$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $w(t)\,(\text{pounds/week})$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $3$ |

Use a left Riemann sum for $w(t)$ over the interval $[0,7]$ with three subintervals to approximate Daniel's total weight loss.
question.worked_solution:
In this case, we have $n=3$ rectangles. Using the left Riemann sum, the area is approximated as

$$
A≈w(0)Δ{t}_{1}+w(1)Δ{t}_{2}+w(3)Δ{t}_{3},
$$

where each $Δ{t}_{i}$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $t$-value and the next one, i.e.,

$$
Δ{t}_{i}={t}_{i+1}-{t}_{i}.
$$

We set up a value table that includes the $Δt$'s.

| $t$ | $0$ | $1$ | $3$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $Δt$ | $1$ | $2$ | $4$ | $-$ |
| $w(t)$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $3$ |

Finally, we plug in the numbers to approximate the area under the curve and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈1\cdot 1+2\cdot 2+1\cdot 4 \\  & =1+4+4 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, in the given context, the area under the curve represents the total weight lost by Daniel. He lost approximately $9$ pounds.
